primary_source.title: AID-Guard: Stateful Authorization for Delegated Agent Effects
primary_source.artifact_release_status: paper states a versioned implementation/evaluation artifact will be released for artifact evaluation; no public code/artifact URL is supplied in v1

verified: AID-Guard's controlled-idempotent contract durably creates one submitted attempt and immutable outbox before dispatch, binds provider idempotency to exact operation scope and request body, returns the durable terminal result on exact replay, fails closed on conflicting reuse, and uses terminal lookup/reconciliation without redispatch.

A root revocation or boundary-epoch change after the submitted-attempt linearization point prevents later authority but does not retroactively cancel the already-submitted request; its result remains attached to the same lineage and must be reconciled rather than resubmitted.

Providers lacking atomic commit or durable exact-result idempotency are explicitly outside the evaluated automatic retry/replacement profile: ambiguity remains charged/uncertain and does not grant automatic retry or replacement.

Reported external-provider counts are internally consistent in the primary paper: 210 Stripe trials = seven 30-trial strata; a separate 30-lineage Stripe recovery campaign canceled the predecessor and committed one successor; 30 overlapping confirm/cancel races produced cancel-win no-charge outcomes; 10 crash-after-cancel schedules blocked successor until provider lookup recovered terminal no-effect, then one successor committed; 10 Resend lineages used the analogous sequential contract without duplicate delivery.

The paper explicitly limits these finite observations: they do not establish arbitrary Stripe linearizability, and the one-effect property is conditional on the declared provider contracts, effect-path inventory, retention windows, and trusted authority/effect boundary.
scope: The worker's separation between REPLAY_RECORDED_RESULT and REDISPATCH_EFFECT is supported in principle by AID-Guard, but only for a durable submitted lineage with exact operation/body identity and a retained authoritative terminal result. It must not be generalized to arbitrary cached text/result replay or to providers without the required idempotent terminal-result contract.

AID-Guard does not show that current authorization is irrelevant in general. It shows that later revocation does not rewrite an already-linearized submission, whose terminal result is reconciled on the existing lineage; new provider dispatch/replacement remains separately gated.

The exact trial counts are primary-paper observations, not an independently replayed artifact result in this audit. The paper says the versioned artifact will be released for artifact evaluation, so implementation-level reproduction remains unavailable from the v1 public surface inspected here.

The worker's 100,000 synthetic episodes and concrete-event witness are worker-local mechanism studies; AID-Guard supports lifecycle distinctions but does not validate that synthetic controller as an integrated system.
downstream_implication: Treat recorded terminal-result replay as a non-redispatch reconciliation class only when exact submitted-attempt lineage, operation/body identity, durable terminal-result retention, and provider contract are positively verified. Unknown/missing response remains ambiguous, not retry permission; a new provider effect requires its own current effect authority or certified-no-effect successor path.
exact_next_action: Rotate to another under-audited C26 namespace. Keep AID-Guard at primary-paper-verified / executable-artifact-unreproduced status until its promised versioned artifact is public, then bind and replay the provider-contract schedules before upgrading reproducibility.
